name: Example: Evaluating a Definite Integral Using Multiple Properties of Definite Integrals
problem:
Suppose that $f(x)$ is a  function such that ${\displaystyle \int_4^1 2 \, f(x) \, \textrm dx = -1}$ 
and ${\displaystyle \int_{1}^{-1} f(x) \, \textrm dx = 2}.$  What is the value of ${\displaystyle \int_{-1}^4 f(x) \, \textrm dx}?$
worked_solution:
Let's simplify the first given integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{1}2\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-1 \\ 2{\int }_{4}^{1}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-1 \\ -2{\int }_{1}^{4}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-1 \\ {\int }_{1}^{4}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The second integral can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =2 \\ -{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =2 \\ {\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
